finding: In the vendored browser harness, sanitize_dom_text() — the module's own prompt-injection guard — is never called by any production code path. Only cli_anything/browser/tests/test_security.py exercises it. Every byte of DOM text returned by fs ls / cat / grep reaches the calling agent unfiltered. validate_url() IS wired (core/page.py:40); the sanitizer is not.
evidence: grep -rn 'sanitize_dom_text' over integrations/cli-anything-harnesses/browser/agent-harness/cli_anything/browser returns only utils/security.py (the definition) and tests/test_security.py (21 call sites). No call from browser_cli.py, core/fs.py, core/page.py, core/session.py or utils/domshell_backend.py. Upstream SECURITY.md names prompt-injected agents as an explicit threat model, which makes the dead guard more surprising, not less.
fix: Do not treat DOM text from a harness as trusted input. The durable fix is upstream (call the sanitizer in domshell_backend._parse_execute_result); locally, the ECC security review should decide whether Steven's agents may act on harness output without a human read. Not fixed here: changing it would modify vendored third-party source and break the 'unmodified' provenance claim.
halt: No — reporting only. An upstream code change is a separate, reviewable decision.

finding: The browser harness spawns 'npx -p @apireno/domshell domshell-proxy' with NO version pin. npx resolves and executes whatever version the npm registry serves at call time, downloading it on first run. This is third-party code fetched and run at each invocation on the Mac that holds client files, and it is outside this repo's control.
evidence: utils/domshell_backend.py:41 DEFAULT_SERVER_CMD = 'npx'; :53-58 _build_server_args() returns ['-p','@apireno/domshell','domshell-proxy','--port',port,'--token',token]. The module docstring at :129-131 states 'The first run may download the package (10-50 MB).' No lockfile, no integrity hash, no version constraint anywhere in the package.
fix: Pin the version at the call site (npx -p @apireno/domshell@<exact> ) or pre-install it with a lockfile and point the harness at the local binary. Until then, treat every harness run as executing an unreviewed npm package. This belongs in the ECC security review alongside F-S1-10.
halt: No — reporting only. Pinning means editing vendored source; raise it upstream or carry a documented patch.

finding: DOMSHELL_TOKEN is passed to the child process as an argv element ('--token', token). Process arguments are world-readable via ps on macOS, so any local process can read the DOMShell auth token while the harness is running.
evidence: utils/domshell_backend.py:57 '--token', token — where token comes from os.environ.get('DOMSHELL_TOKEN','') at :45. Contrast with the port, which is not sensitive. An env-var or stdin hand-off would not appear in ps.
fix: Prefer an environment hand-off to the child over argv. Single-user Mac lowers the impact but does not remove it. MAC-SETUP.sh's new step reports DOMSHELL_TOKEN as NEEDS-STEVEN and never reads, writes or guesses it.
halt: Yes — the token's value is a credential. The installer creates no skeleton for it and never touches it.

finding: Upstream HKUDS/CLI-Anything is internally inconsistent about its licence. browser/agent-harness/setup.py declares license="MIT" and an OSI MIT classifier, but the repository LICENSE file is the Apache License 2.0 verbatim, and both the root README.md and the harness's own cli_anything/browser/README.md say 'Apache License 2.0'.
evidence: setup.py:29 license="MIT" and classifier 'License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License'; LICENSE is 201 lines of Apache 2.0 (sha256 0cff1a8ac2a381870a2c57cbe9b25f95bea0925b39b7fbf6a04ec23df7c77760); README.md:1799 'Apache License 2.0'; cli_anything/browser/README.md:264 'Apache License 2.0 — See CLI-Anything for details.'
fix: We treat Apache 2.0 as governing, because that is what the actual LICENSE file contains and what two READMEs state, and it is the stricter of the two on attribution. The full text is vendored at integrations/cli-anything-harnesses/browser/agent-harness/LICENSE; upstream ships no NOTICE file, so there is none to carry; the setup.py string is left exactly as upstream wrote it because the tree is unmodified. Recorded in VENDORED.md.
halt: No — this is a documentation call, not a legal interpretation. Apache 2.0 obligations are met either way.

finding: The browser harness's private-network blocking is OFF by default, so a prompt-injected or mistaken agent can drive the browser at localhost, RFC-1918 addresses and link-local (including 169.254.169.254). The flag is also read at import time, so exporting it after the process starts has no effect.
evidence: utils/security.py:22 _BLOCK_PRIVATE_NETWORKS = os.environ.get('CLI_ANYTHING_BROWSER_BLOCK_PRIVATE','').lower() in ('true','1') — module scope, and the comment says 'Default: False (allow localhost/private networks for development)'. The _PRIVATE_NETWORK_PATTERNS list at :54-73 is complete but only consulted when that flag is true (:150).
fix: Set CLI_ANYTHING_BROWSER_BLOCK_PRIVATE=true in the shell profile AND in the runner task env before the harness process starts. MAC-SETUP.sh's new step prints this recommendation every run; it does not set it, because an export inside the installer would not survive the run.
halt: No — a one-line env change Steven makes in his own profile.

finding: The harness REPL creates ~/.cli-anything-<software>/ and writes plaintext command history into it. On a machine holding client files that history will accumulate browser-automation commands, and those commands carry URLs — MLS numbers, listing addresses, portal paths. It is a write outside the working directory, made simply by constructing the REPL skin.
evidence: utils/repl_skin.py:160-163 hist_dir = Path.home()/f'.cli-anything-{self.software}'; hist_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); self.history_file = str(hist_dir/'history'), consumed by FileHistory(self.history_file) at :494. Verified separately that --help does NOT construct the skin: running --help on all eight binaries against a clean HOME created 0 files, so mac-verify.sh's read-only guarantee is intact.
fix: Treat ~/.cli-anything-*/history as client data for backup, disk-encryption and retention purposes. Do not copy it into the repo, the vector index or the knowledge graph.
halt: Yes if any of that history is ever moved — client PII entering the vector index or knowledge graph is a HALT row.

finding: On construction the REPL skin walks every ancestor of its own installed location looking for skills/<skill-id>/SKILL.md, stating directories up to the filesystem root. The result is stored on self.skill_path and then never displayed or read, so it is dead computation with a filesystem-probe side effect rather than an injection path.
evidence: utils/repl_skin.py:147-156 iterates Path(__file__).resolve().parents and breaks on the first candidate that is_file(). grep for 'skill_path' across the package shows assignment at :156 and nothing else; the banner at :233-234 prints skill_install_cmd and global_skill_path only. No read_text() anywhere in the module.
fix: No action. Recorded so a future reviewer does not mistake the walk for a live skill-loading path, and so it is on record if upstream ever starts reading that file.

finding: homes, showingtime and showami declared cli-anything-browser>=1.0.0 — a distribution that is not on PyPI and was not vendored — and imported cli_anything.browser.core at module level. From this repo alone they could not be installed or tested: pip install . failed with 'No matching distribution found', and with --no-deps their --help exited 1 and pytest aborted at collection. Four of seven packages worked standalone; three did not. It was papered over by MAC-SETUP.sh git-cloning HKUDS/CLI-Anything first, which made the repo's own tests unrunnable in CI or on a second machine.
evidence: setup.py of all three lists 'cli-anything-browser>=1.0.0',   # not on PyPI: install browser/agent-harness first. Closed by vendoring browser/agent-harness into the repo: in one clean venv all eight now install from local paths, all eight --help exit 0, and pytest gives 623 passed / 41 skipped (browser 195+11, homes 67+8, showingtime 70+11, showami 70+11, skyslope 71, zipforms 70, lofty 37, zoho 43).
fix: Vendored at integrations/cli-anything-harnesses/browser/agent-harness (Apache-2.0, byte-identical to upstream commit 34f5195, provenance in VENDORED.md). New MAC-SETUP.sh step cli-anything-harnesses installs all eight from the repo in one uv command with browser first. New mac-verify.sh section checks all eight.

finding: The instruction to assert that 'grep -qw act on the help output finds nothing' for each of the eight cannot hold: the browser ENGINE genuinely ships an act command group with act click and act type. That is DOMShell's write surface and the reason the engine exists. Applying the blanket rule would either fail the verifier permanently or require pretending the write surface is absent.
evidence: cli-anything-browser --help lists: act, fs, page, repl, session. browser_cli.py:308-336 defines @cli.group() act with act_click and act_type. The seven site harnesses have no act verb — confirmed by word match against all seven real --help outputs. MAC-SETUP.sh's cli-anything step already states the policy: 'REFUSED here: any act click / act type verb in a generated harness'. The policy is about GENERATED SITE harnesses, not the engine.
fix: mac-verify.sh implements the rule as written for the seven site harnesses (act present = FAIL, the read-only guarantee) and reports the engine's act group by name on every run as an explicit info line rather than passing it silently or failing forever. The installer step prints the same warning. Flagged here because it is a deliberate, documented deviation from the literal instruction.
halt: No — but Steven should confirm the split reading is what he wants before the ECC review signs off.

finding: A substring check (grep -q act) false-positives on all seven site harnesses, reporting a write surface on harnesses that have none. The word match is not an edge-case nicety; it is the difference between the check working and the check being noise.
evidence: Measured against the eight real --help outputs 2026-09-22: 'interactive' appears in all seven site harnesses, 'action' in skyslope and zipforms, 'redact'/'redacted' in lofty and zoho. grep -q act matches every one; grep -qw act matches none of them and does match the browser engine's real act group. Recipe names one level down (showingtime's my-listing-activity) are the same trap.
fix: mac-verify.sh uses grep -qw act throughout, with the measured word list recorded in a comment above the check so the next editor does not 'simplify' it back.

area: Pre-existing lint (NOT introduced or fixed here)
finding: shellcheck reports SC2015 at MAC-SETUP.sh:439, in the whatsapp-cli step: 'run mkdir -p "$BINDIR" && run ln -sf ... || true'. A && B || C is not if-then-else, so a failing ln is swallowed and a failing mkdir still yields success. The net effect matches the intended best-effort behaviour, so it is informational.
evidence: Confirmed pre-existing: git show HEAD:MAC-SETUP.sh | shellcheck reports the same single SC2015 at the same line 439, before any of this work. It is the only shellcheck finding remaining in either script. mac-verify.sh is shellcheck-clean at exit 0.
fix: Left alone deliberately — it is in another engineer's step and changing it alters that step's error handling without being asked. Flagged so the next owner of the whatsapp-cli step can decide.

finding: The zoho harness reads ~/.config/zoho/.env for five variable names, but nothing in MAC-SETUP.sh created that skeleton — lofty-keyfile covers Lofty and the cli-anything step covers the three browser sites, leaving Zoho with no file to fill in.
evidence: zoho/agent-harness/cli_anything/zoho/utils/zoho_backend.py:32-35 ENV_FILE = '~/.config/zoho/.env'; FILE_VARS = (ZOHO_ACCOUNTS_URL, ZOHO_API_URL, ZOHO_CLIENT_ID, ZOHO_CLIENT_SECRET, ZOHO_REFRESH_TOKEN). No ensure_env_file zoho existed anywhere in MAC-SETUP.sh before this change.
fix: The new cli-anything-harnesses step calls ensure_env_file zoho with those five NAMES and no values, chmod 600, never rewriting an existing file. Zoho's actual blocker remains the profile-level 'Zoho CRM API Access' toggle, which the step reports as NEEDS-STEVEN rather than attempting.
halt: Yes for the values and for the profile toggle — a credential and an account permission change. The installer only ever writes names.

area: Test coverage / what is still untested
finding: All 41 skipped tests are live-browser or live-site E2E tests that need DOMShell running, the Chrome extension installed and a signed-in session on the Mac. None of them has executed anywhere — not in this run, and not by the scripts' authors. The installer and verifier changes have likewise never run on macOS.
evidence: Skip reasons: browser 11 x 'DOMShell E2E tests are disabled or DOMShell MCP server not available. Set DOMSHELL_E2E=1'; homes 8, showingtime 11, showami 11 x 'live <site> tests are opt-in: set CLI_ANYTHING_<SITE>_LIVE=1 on the Mac with DOMShell running and a signed-in session' (plus a few per-site recipe-shape skips). skyslope, zipforms, lofty and zoho skip nothing. MAC-SETUP.sh and mac-verify.sh both carry the header 'Not executed on a Mac by its author'.
fix: Nothing to fix — stated so it is not mistaken for coverage. The non-dry-run install path, the symlink creation, the zoho .env creation, and every harness check against a real ~/Applications/cli-anything-harnesses venv have only been exercised via a simulated HOME on Linux.
halt: No — but nothing here substitutes for one supervised run on the Mac.
